record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: If the Roberge-Weiss endpoint is first order for some parameter regime, does the associated first-order line extend until it meets the crossover line and terminate at another critical endpoint, and can that additional endpoint be identified explicitly in lattice QCD? More broadly, can such an endpoint serve as a controlled testing ground for methods intended to detect critical points without facing the real-density sign problem?

evidence.quote: If the RW endpoint is a first-order transition, the first-order phase transition line extends to the crossover line. Then, another endpoint will appear somewhere. However, such a new critical point has not been confirmed by the lattice QCD simulation.
Such a critical point may be a good testing ground for the determination of critical points avoiding the sign problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice QCD at imaginary baryon chemical potential μ = iμ_I with μ_I/T fixed at the Roberge–Weiss (RW) value π (mod 2π/3), where the theory exhibits the Z_3-related Roberge–Weiss first-order transition in the Polyakov-loop phase as a function of temperature T. Let T_RW denote the temperature at which the RW transition terminates (the RW endpoint). It is known that, depending on the number of flavors and the values of the quark masses, the RW endpoint can be a triple point of first-order type (in the small-mass or large-mass corners of the Columbia-plot extension) rather than a second-order endpoint.

Suppose the RW endpoint is first order. Then the first-order line emanating from the RW endpoint at μ_I/T = π extends into the (T, μ_I) plane and must meet the analytic-crossover line of the QCD finite-temperature transition. At that meeting point one expects an additional critical endpoint (a second-order endpoint terminating the first-order line where it joins the crossover region).

(a) Establish, in lattice QCD with physical or near-physical quark content, the existence of this additional critical endpoint when the RW endpoint is first order, and determine its location (T*, μ_I*) and universality class.

(b) Since this endpoint lies at imaginary chemical potential, the fermion determinant is real and the standard sign problem is absent. Develop and validate, on this endpoint, methods for the identification of critical points (e.g. finite-size scaling, Lee–Yang zeros, Binder cumulants, or other criticality detectors) that are intended to be transferred to the search for the conjectured QCD critical endpoint at real baryon chemical potential without confronting the sign problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that while the order of the Roberge–Weiss endpoint itself has been extensively studied (first order in large/small mass regions, 3D Ising for intermediate masses, with T_RW ≈ 208(5) MeV at physical point), the existence and location of the additional critical endpoint where the first-order RW line meets the crossover line has not been confirmed by lattice QCD simulations. No recent publication appears to have explicitly identified this secondary endpoint, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Roberge-Weiss endpoint at the physical point of QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Continuum-extrapolated T_RW=208(5) MeV; finite-size scaling consistent with 3D Ising universality class at the physical point.
status_evidence.claim: RW endpoint nature at physical point is studied but the additional endpoint where the first-order line meets the crossover line is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Order of the Roberge-Weiss endpoint (finite size transition) in QCD
status_evidence.snippet: RW endpoint is first order at small and large quark masses, second order in an intermediate range.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms first-order RW endpoint regimes exist, the regime in which the conjectured additional endpoint should be searched for.

status_evidence.title: The nature of the Roberge-Weiss Transition in Nf=2 QCD with Wilson Fermions
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates order of RW endpoint without confirming a secondary critical endpoint along the first-order line.
status_evidence.claim: No identification of an additional critical endpoint joining the crossover line is reported.
